background.text: What D2 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: When a property owner confirms the deletion of a property, the platform must remove the property record from the database.

rules.text: WHEN a Property Owner initiates property deletion, THE Platform SHALL prompt for confirmation before proceeding
rules.reading: Whenever a Property Owner initiates the deletion process for a property, the Platform must display a confirmation prompt before proceeding with the deletion.

rules.text: WHEN a Property Owner confirms deletion, THE Platform SHALL remove the Property record from the Platform
rules.reading: In any situation where a Property Owner confirms the deletion, the Property record must be removed from the Platform's active data set.

rules.text: WHEN a Property is deleted, THE Platform SHALL display a confirmation message and redirect to the properties list
rules.reading: When a Property is deleted, the Platform must display a confirmation message and redirect the user to the properties list.

rules.text: THE Platform SHALL implement soft deletion to retain Property records in the database for audit purposes while hiding them from the user interface
rules.reading: The platform must implement soft deletion by ensuring that when a property deletion is completed, the property record remains present in the database and is not visible in the user interface.

alternative.reading: The system must retain property records in the database and hide them from the user interface to implement soft deletion for audit purposes.

rules.text: WHEN a Property Owner attempts to delete a Property that does not belong to their User Account, THE Platform SHALL deny the deletion and display an authorization error message
rules.reading: If a Property Owner attempts to delete a Property that does not belong to their User Account, the Platform must deny the deletion and display an authorization error message.
